title: Coverage Tenure Down Payment Share for Seller Settlements
content:
**Rule.** On a spread failed-sale charge of a Real Estate Service Contracts listing order, the down payment taken from the seller reflects how long the seller has held Bridgewell coverage. Tenure is counted as the whole months from the start date of the seller's earliest-started Utility Line Protection Plans plan or Homeowner Service Contracts contract in status active to the settlement date.

| Tenure | Tenure share |
|---|---|
| fewer than 6 whole months, or no such active plan or contract | 25% |
| at least 6 but fewer than 24 whole months | 10% |
| 24 whole months or more | no tenure share |

The tenure share is added once to the down payment share. The down payment is the open failed-sale balance times the down payment share, which is never below zero, rounded to the cent, and it is taken with the first settlement payment.

## Boundaries (hypothetical tenures)

| Whole months since the earliest active start date | Tenure share |
|---|---|
| 5 | 25% |
| 6 | 10% |
| 23 | 10% |
| 24 | none |

## Points of judgement (hypothetical sellers)

- An active line plan started 14 whole months ago and an active homeowner contract started 30 whole months ago: the earliest-started is the homeowner contract, 30 months, so no tenure share.
- A seller whose only line plan was cancelled and who holds no homeowner contract: no active plan or contract, so 25%.
